subsystems.name: Problem encoding layer
subsystems.role: turns linear-programming or semidefinite-programming data into a form the quantum processor can work on.
parts: state-preparation circuits for the objective and right-hand-side vectors

subsystems.name: Quantum linear-system solver
subsystems.role: computes the Newton direction by inverting a linear system once per iteration.

subsystems.name: Classical outer loop
subsystems.role: runs the barrier method that ties the quantum calls together.

subsystems.name: Readout and solution extraction
subsystems.role: converts quantum amplitudes back into numbers the classical loop can use.
parts: sparse access to the direction vector

subsystems.name: Quantum data memory
subsystems.role: serves matrix and vector entries to the processor in superposition.

subsystems.name: Fault-tolerant processor
subsystems.role: executes the deep, error-corrected circuits the method needs.

buildSteps.title: Write the problem in a solver-friendly form
buildSteps.detail: Express the task as a linear program (minimise a linear objective subject to linear equalities and non-negativity) or a semidefinite program. Sparsity, conditioning and dimension decide whether the quantum route is even plausible.

buildSteps.title: Compile the data into block-encodings
buildSteps.detail: Build circuits that encode the constraint matrix, objective and right-hand side as block-encodings — sub-blocks of larger unitaries — so that quantum linear algebra can act on them.

buildSteps.title: Prepare a starting state
buildSteps.detail: Amplitude-encode an initial point on the central path. This state preparation is usually the single largest cost in the whole algorithm.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the Newton system
buildSteps.detail: Form the normal-equations matrix for the current iterate as a block-encoding. Solving this matrix for the Newton direction is the core quantum subroutine.

buildSteps.title: Run the quantum solve
buildSteps.detail: Apply quantum singular value transformation (or an HHL-type inversion) with amplitude amplification to produce a state proportional to the Newton direction.

buildSteps.title: Extract the direction classically
buildSteps.detail: Use tomography or amplitude estimation to learn enough digits of the direction to update the classical loop — precision here is where costs multiply.

buildSteps.title: Update and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Classically reduce the barrier parameter, keep the iterate inside the feasible region, and repeat until the duality gap falls below the target tolerance.

buildSteps.title: Read out and verify
buildSteps.detail: Sample the final state, reconstruct an approximate solution, round it to feasibility and compare the objective and runtime against a tuned classical solver.

prerequisites.why: the circuits are far deeper than any noisy machine can run, and the error-correction overhead is very large.
the polynomial speedups assume reading matrix entries in superposition; only small proof-of-concept devices exist, none error-corrected.

prerequisites.tech: Efficient state preparation for structured matrices
prerequisites.why: small demonstrations exist, but circuit cost grows rapidly with matrix size and required precision.
run on tiny systems on real hardware, but their cost scales with the condition number and the inverse of precision.

prerequisites.tech: Classical interior-point methods and dequantisation analysis
prerequisites.why: the baseline is a mature classical field, and some claimed quantum speedups disappear when equivalent data-access assumptions are given to classical algorithms.

pathway.milestone: theory and small-scale primitives: QSVT compiled for toy linear systems on a handful of qubits
pathway.unlocks: a clearer map of which problem classes could plausibly benefit.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant demonstration that block-encodes a structured matrix of useful size and performs one Newton step end-to-end
pathway.unlocks: evidence that subroutine costs behave as the theory predicts.

pathway.milestone: a full interior-point run on a small but non-trivial linear or semidefinite program, benchmarked against a tuned classical solver
pathway.unlocks: identification of the narrow problem class, if any, where the quantum route wins.

pathway.milestone: demonstrated end-to-end advantage on a real logistics or finance problem that survives dequantisation critiques
pathway.unlocks: a practical optimisation tool rather than a theoretical curiosity.
